overview: The City Council held its 2026 organizational meeting to elect leadership and address a controversial change in the city's ambulance service provider. The Council also authorized infrastructure funding and confirmed an Acting City Clerk following a vacancy in the office.

items.title: Election of Council President and Vice President
items.summary: Zac Bears was elected Council President and Emily Lazzaro was elected Vice President for the 2026 term. Both members were sworn into office by the Assistant City Clerk.

items.title: Appointment of City Messenger
items.summary: The Council discussed redefining the vacant City Messenger role to include constituent services before tabling the matter.

items.title: Procedural Resolutions and Approval of Records
items.summary: Approved the adoption of standing committee rules, the transfer of pending papers from 2025 to 2026, and the meeting records from December 16, 2025.

items.title: Planning and Permitting Committee Report
items.summary: Approved a committee report regarding a draft condominium conversion ordinance intended to establish a regulatory process for multi-unit conversions.

items.title: Review of Ambulance/EMS Contract Transition
items.summary: Referred a resolution to the Committee of the Whole to investigate the administration's decision to switch the city's emergency medical provider from Armstrong Ambulance to Cataldo Ambulance. Discussion focused on transparency, response times, and claims of retaliation against the unionized incumbent provider, while public safety officials defended the change as a strategic service improvement.

items.title: Common Victualler Licenses
items.summary: Approved licenses for Wunder HDR Holdings at Station Landing and Colwyn Management for the Medford Hyatt Place.

items.title: Confirmation of Acting City Clerk
items.summary: Confirmed Richard Alicio, Jr. as Acting City Clerk following the resignation of the previous clerk and approved an amendment to provide him with pay commensurate with the permanent position.

items.title: Support for SMFA Professors at Tufts University
items.summary: Approved a resolution standing in solidarity with Tufts University School of the Museum of Fine Arts professors seeking a fair contract.

items.title: City Services on Private Ways
items.summary: Approved a resolution to hold a public forum and draft an informational guide regarding the delivery of city services on private ways. The Council also requested a legal memorandum to clarify municipal authority under state law for maintaining non-public streets.

items.title: Wage Adjustments for DPW, Recreation, and Building Unions
items.summary: Waived the three readings and ordained wage adjustments for several city unions through 2027.

items.title: Capital Stabilization Fund Appropriations
items.summary: Approved $37,223 for a hybrid DPW vehicle and $325,000 for the design of water main replacements on various city streets.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Residents addressed the Council regarding permit parking fees in the Green Line Extension zone, sidewalk maintenance at Route 60, and mental health strain on emergency services.
